subject: Clarification on co-sell settlement routing, W-8/W-9 and VAT handling across AWS/Azure/GCP
messages:
From: Lisa Cheng <lisa.cheng@amazon.com>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: aws-marketplace-billing@amazon.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Quick question on co-sell settlements / tax flow for AcmeCorp

Hi Dev,

Thanks for the quick intake call earlier. As we move AcmeCorp into the co-sell pathway, our finance team asked for a clear mapping of how Redwood wants invoices to flow and what tax documents you need on file. Two specific asks from AWS side:

- For US customers transacting via AWS Marketplace SaaS Contracts, do you want AWS to invoice the end-customer and then route a consolidated partner settlement to Redwood, or should Redwood issue direct invoices to AcmeCorp and have AWS only handle marketplace fees?
- For international subsidiaries (Acme has an EU entity), they asked whether Redwood will accept reverse-charge VAT on an EU entity invoice or if AWS needs to handle VAT collection in the marketplace billing.

Can you confirm required tax docs for partner payout (W-9 vs W-8BEN-E) and whether we should expect separate settlement invoices per entity or a single parent-level settlement? If you have a short mapping matrix or template, that would help speed approvals on our side.

Thanks,
Lisa
Senior Partner Ops, AWS Marketplace

--
Lisa Cheng
Amazon Web Services

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Cheng <lisa.cheng@amazon.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, aws-marketplace-billing@amazon.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick question on co-sell settlements / tax flow for AcmeCorp

Lisa — thanks, great questions. Looping in Lauren and Marcus from Finance/Marketplace to confirm details and provide the mapping. High-level answers below; will follow up with a filled template.

- Preferred flow: Redwood prefers AWS to collect end-customer payments via the marketplace (SaaS contract), and then AWS issues a settlement invoice to Redwood (partner payout) net of marketplace fees. This keeps customer billing consistent across customers and simplifies collections.
- Multi-entity note: For customers with EU entities, Redwood can accept EU-entity invoices *if* Acme provides a VAT number and the invoice is billed to that EU entity. In that case, Redwood expects the EU entity invoice to use reverse-charge where applicable; otherwise, AWS can collect VAT on the marketplace transaction depending on the marketplace rules per country.
- Tax docs for payout: Redwood needs partner tax certification for the paying entity that will receive settlement (W-9 for US entities, W-8BEN-E for foreign entities). If Redwood is receiving aggregated payouts on a US legal entity, we will provide a W-9 for that entity. If payouts go to a non-US subsidiary, that subsidiary must supply W-8BEN-E.

I'll attach a mapping template and an example W-8 we usually accept. Lauren / Marcus — can you add any controls or exceptions we should flag for AWS?

Best,
Dev
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Marketplace_Settlement_Playbook.docx (see attached)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick question on co-sell settlements / tax flow for AcmeCorp

Adding a few controls from Finance:

- Settlement granularity: we prefer one settlement per legal entity per month to keep revenue recognition clean. If AWS can produce per-entity settlement invoices (Entity A, Entity B) that maps to our chart of accounts, great. If AWS only does parent-level settlements, we will need a reliable ledger report from AWS that splits charges by customer legal entity so we can attribute revenue appropriately.

- Withholding: For any non-US payout recipients, confirm whether AWS applies any withholding on the marketplace payout. Redwood will rely on the receiving entity's tax status (W-8BEN-E) to determine withholding; if AWS withholds, we need a withholding certificate or remittance detail.

- VAT: For EU reverse-charge, we require (1) customer VAT ID on the invoice, (2) invoice explicitly stating reverse-charge or zero VAT under local law, and (3) supporting contract/PO referencing the EU legal entity. If AWS is collecting VAT, please confirm the VAT rate applied and provide the VAT invoice copy in the settlement packet.

I attached a filled Invoice_Mapping_Template_v2.xlsx we use internally — please populate columns A-D with the Acme entity names, billing addresses, VAT/Tax IDs, and desired payout entity. Marcus — confirm if we need any additional fields for audit.

-Lauren
Finance Director, Redwood Inference

Lisa / Rajiv — following up with the attached artifacts and our proposed playbook. Summary action items below and attached files for your finance teams.

Summary / Ask:
1) Please confirm AWS settlement capability: can AWS emit distinct settlement invoices per Redwood-designated payout entity (yes/no)? If no, provide the detailed ledger export format and cadence so Redwood Finance can map to legal entities.
2) Acme: please complete the attached Invoice_Mapping_Template_v2.xlsx and indicate which legal entity will accept Redwood invoices vs AWS invoices. Include VAT IDs for any EU entities.
3) AWS: confirm whether marketplace will apply VAT at checkout for Acme's EU purchases or if you will rely on reverse-charge; if VAT is applied, please include VAT invoice copies in the settlement bundle.
4) Tax forms: Redwood will provide a W-9 for US payout entities; if AWS is routing payouts to a non-US subsidiary, please request W-8BEN-E from that subsidiary and share a copy with Redwood Finance prior to the first settlement cycle.

Attachments included in this thread: Invoice_Mapping_Template_v2.xlsx; Marketplace_Settlement_Playbook.docx; Signed_W8BEN-E_Example.pdf

If helpful, we can schedule 30 minutes this week with Finance ops to walk through the template and close these items.

Thanks — looking forward to closing the final mapping.

Best,
